---
title: "Global Pol II footprint-positive LCL clustering"
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true
params:
  output: null
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
cfg <- yaml::read_yaml(file.path(params$output, "run_config.yaml"))
here <- file.path(cfg$project, "code/pausing/clustering_Pol2")
source(file.path(here, "pol2_clustering_functions.R"))
source(file.path(here, "pol2_clustering_plots.R"))
pol2_load_helpers(cfg$project)
x <- readRDS(file.path(params$output, "tables", "clustering.rds"))
annotation <- readRDS(file.path(params$output, "tables", "annotations.rds"))
m <- annotation$molecules
fp <- annotation$footprints
res <- pol2_heatmap_result(x, annotation, cfg$heatmap_max_reads, cfg$seed)
sample_colors <- pol2_sample_colors(cfg, res$assignments$sample_name)
clusters <- levels(res$assignments$cluster)
k <- length(clusters)
```

This is one global clustering across all configured LCL samples. Each included molecule
fully spans the window (−1000 to +999 bp) of a FANTOM5 dominant TSS that lies in a Pol II
IDR peak, and carries at least one 30–60 bp FiberHMM v2 footprint, from its own sample's
`recalled_tf` calls, overlapping that window.
Duplicate footprint records are counted once. Other molecules do not enter clustering.
Denominators use observed m6A sites across all full-window
molecules at each TSS, before random sampling.

The analysis contains `r nrow(m)` randomly selected molecules, out of
`r x$eligible_molecules` eligible ones, from `r uniqueN(m$sample_name)` contributing
samples and `r uniqueN(m$tss_id)` TSSs.
Up to 5,000 unique sample/read molecules are drawn without replacement from all samples
combined, using seed 1. When a molecule qualifies at multiple TSSs, one eligible TSS
is randomly selected for that molecule. Cluster fractions describe this random sample
of the selected population, not all TSS-spanning molecules or cells.
The footprint criterion is candidate evidence for Pol II association, not protein identification.

Clusters are shown in order of their median pausing index (Day 2016 PI from
`pause_index.tsv`, joined by Ensembl gene ID; each TSS counted once per cluster), lowest first.

```{r heatmap, fig.width=14, fig.height=11 + 0.55 * k}
pol2_draw_heatmap(pol2_molecule_heatmap(res, sample_colors), clusters, profiles = TRUE)
```

```{r profiles, fig.width=10, fig.height=1.4 * k + 2.5}
pol2_plot_profiles(annotation)
```

Heatmap, average profiles with the median PI, and bulk Pol II ChIP fold-enrichment over
each molecule's TSS region (−50 to +299 bp; log2 of the cluster mean over the mean of all
molecules, Wilcoxon test of the cluster against all others, BH over clusters), in the
layout of Fig. 1c of the nano-NOMe-seq paper.

```{r fig1c, fig.width=16, fig.height=max(7, 0.9 * k + 2)}
pol2_fig1c(res, annotation, sample_colors)
```

```{r summary}
knitr::kable(annotation$summary, digits = 3)
```

```{r footprints, fig.width=10, fig.height=1.4 * k + 2.5}
pol2_plot_footprints(annotation)
```

Each molecule's 30–60 bp footprints, one row per molecule in the heatmap's order.

```{r footprint-molecules, fig.width=9, fig.height=11 + 0.55 * k}
pol2_plot_footprint_molecules(res, annotation)
```

Pol II fold-enrichment is measured over each candidate footprint. The boxplot
summarizes a molecule's footprints first, to avoid giving molecules with several
footprints extra weight. Bulk Pol II signal is shared locus evidence, not an independent
measurement of polymerase binding on each molecule.

```{r signal, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
signal <- fp[, .(signal = if (all(is.na(pol2_mean))) NA_real_ else mean(pol2_mean, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(cluster, observation_id)]
ggplot(signal, aes(cluster, signal)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Cluster", y = "Mean Pol II fold-enrichment across candidate footprints")
```

PI is joined by Ensembl gene ID; the RefSeq TSS of `pause_index.tsv` can differ from the
FANTOM5 TSS used here.

```{r pi, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
pi_sites <- unique(m[, .(cluster, tss_id, pi)])
if (any(is.finite(pi_sites$pi))) {
  print(ggplot(pi_sites[is.finite(pi)], aes(cluster, pi)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
          scale_y_log10() + theme_bw() + labs(y = "PI (one value per TSS within each cluster)"))
} else cat("No matching PI values have been supplied.")
```
